Context: the studio had been assembling hourly invoices from raw timesheets;
reconciliation cost Lorna a day per month.

Options considered: hourly billing from raw timesheets; flat monthly billing
per client.

Decision: Ledgerline moves to flat monthly billing per client, agreed in the
pricing discussion (m-003) — clients see one predictable number; timesheets
stay internal for capacity planning.

Consequences: invoicing is a one-step monthly run; scope creep now surfaces
in planning, not on the invoice.

The pricing discussion weighed hourly billing assembled from raw timesheets
against flat monthly billing per client: hourly recovers every scrap of
effort but costs Lorna a reconciliation day each month and reads
unpredictably to clients; flat monthly is one predictable number per client
with timesheets kept internal for capacity planning. Flat monthly won, and
d-005 landed three days later.

final_answer:
The Ledgerline pricing discussion (meeting m-003) evaluated two options: **hourly billing from raw timesheets** versus **flat monthly billing per client**. The discussion highlighted that hourly billing "recovers every scrap of effort but costs Lorna a reconciliation day each month and reads unpredictably to clients," while flat monthly provides "one predictable number per client with timesheets kept internal for capacity planning" (m-003). Flat monthly won, and three days later the decision d-005 formalized it: "Ledgerline moves to flat monthly billing per client... clients see one predictable number; timesheets stay internal for capacity planning" (d-005). The consequence was that "invoicing is a one-step monthly run; scope creep now surfaces in planning, not on the invoice" (d-005).
